candidates.attacker_control: The `/DecodeParms` dictionary of any stream object in an untrusted PDF is fully attacker-controlled (COSDictionary parsed from the file). Setting `/Predictor > 1` together with `/Columns 0` (or `/Colors 0`, or `/BitsPerComponent 0`) yields a zero row length. The stream body only needs to inflate/LZW-decode to at least one byte so that `FlateFilter.decompress()` calls `out.write(res, 0, resRead)` with `resRead > 0` (or `LZWFilter.doLZWDecode()` calls `decoded.write(data)`).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Looked for any validation that would prevent the zero-length row: `wrapPredictor` only clamps `colors` upward with `Math.min(..., 32)` (line 289) and has no lower-bound/`> 0` check for colors, bitsPerComponent or columns; `PredictorOutputStream`'s constructor and `write()` contain no `toRead == 0` guard; the `predictorPerRow` branch cannot rescue predictor 2 (or any predictor 2-9). Verified that no exception breaks the loop: `decodePredictorRow(2, 1, 8, 0, byte[0], byte[0])` takes the `bitsPerComponent == 8` path whose `for (p = bytesPerPixel=1; p < rowlength=0; ...)` body never runs; `out.write(byte[0])` and `System.arraycopy(..., 0)` are legal; EOF cannot be reached because the loop never reads input. Also checked the alternative guard patterns in the codebase (e.g. explicit loop protections in `BaseParser.parseDirObject`, `COSParser.parseXref` `/Prev`, `XrefTrailerResolver.setStartxref`) — none of them covers this filter path.
candidates.impact: Denial of service: the thread/JVM handling the PDF hangs in a tight loop with 100% CPU and never returns (and can exhaust the request/worker pool of a server that parses untrusted PDFs). Because XRef/object streams are decoded at load time, a small crafted PDF can hang `PDDocument.load(...)` itself, not just rendering/text extraction. Memory use stays low, making the hang hard to notice via resource caps apart from timeouts.
candidates.prerequisites: An application processes an untrusted PDF with PDFBox (default lenient parsing). The crafted stream must actually be decoded; this is guaranteed for XRef streams and object streams during `PDDocument.load`, and for content/metadata streams whenever the application renders or extracts text. No privileges, passwords, or special configuration are required.
candidates.root_cause: `Predictor.wrapPredictor()` forwards attacker-controlled DecodeParms (`/Colors`, `/BitsPerComponent`, `/Columns`) to `PredictorOutputStream` without validating that the computed row length is > 0. `calculateRowLength()` returns `(columns * colors * bitsPerComponent + 7) / 8`, which is 0 for e.g. `/Columns 0`, `/Colors 0`, or `/BitsPerComponent 0`. The new buffered writer `PredictorOutputStream.write(byte[],int,int)` (lines 345-375) then computes `toRead = Math.min(rowLength - currentRowData, maxOffset - currentOffset) == 0`, copies 0 bytes, leaves `currentOffset`/`currentRowData` unchanged, and because `currentRowData == currentRow.length` (0 == 0) it repeatedly calls `decodeAndWriteRow()`, which writes a zero-length row and flips buffers. Nothing in the loop consumes input, changes state, or throws, so the loop never terminates.
candidates.title: Infinite loop in PDFBox predictor decoding when DecodeParms yields a zero-length row (/Columns 0, /Colors 0 or /BitsPerComponent 0)
candidates.trace: Crafted PDF stream dictionary with `/Filter /FlateDecode /DecodeParms << /Predictor 2 /Columns 0 >>` (or an xref/object stream with the same parameters) -> `COSStream.createInputStream()`/`COSParser.parseCOSStream()` path -> `Filter.decode()` -> `FlateFilter.decode()` line 50 (or `LZWFilter.decode()` line 76) -> `Predictor.wrapPredictor(decoded, decodeParams)` line 284: `colors = min(/Colors=1, 32)`, `bitsPerPixel = /BitsPerComponent=8`, `columns = /Columns=0` -> `new PredictorOutputStream(...)` line 293 -> constructor line 333 computes `rowLength = (0*8 + 7)/8 = 0` and allocates `new byte[0]` rows (lines 335-336) -> first `write(bytes, 0, len>0)` enters the `while (currentOffset < maxOffset)` loop (line 350); `predictorPerRow` is false for predictor 2, so the else branch (line 360) computes `toRead = Math.min(0 - 0, len - 0) = 0`, performs a 0-length `System.arraycopy` (line 363), adds 0 to `currentRowData`/`currentOffset` (lines 364-365), then `currentRowData == currentRow.length` (line 369) is true, so `decodeAndWriteRow()` (line 371) writes an empty array and `flipRows()` resets the state -> identical state every iteration -> CPU spin with no progress and no exit condition. The same zero-progress condition exists in the legacy `Predictor.decodePredictor()` while-loop (lines 223-249) when rowlength is 0 and predictor < 10.
candidates.unverified: Not executed or reproduced (no code execution permitted); the infinite loop is established by source-level state analysis only. The mapping of this defect to the benchmark's specific VUL4J-20 fix/CVE is my inference, not confirmed: several other zero-progress/unbounded loops exist in the same snapshot (see rejected leads), any of which could be the intended target. Also unverified whether other entry points (e.g. `CCITTFaxFilter`) reach this same method in all configurations.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-835 Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') / CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (denial of service)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned snapshot (Apache PDFBox, 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, VUL4J-20) using source text plus the partial P1 index. Focused reading: `pdfbox` core `cos/`, `pdfparser/` (COSParser, BaseParser, PDFStreamParser, PDFXrefStreamParser, PDFObjectStreamParser, XrefTrailerResolver), `filter/` (Flate, LZW, Predictor, CCITT, ASCII/others by inspection), `contentstream/` (PDFStreamEngine, operators), `pdmodel/` fonts (PDFont, PDType0Font, PDFontFactory, encodings), functions (PDFunctionType0/3/4 and type4 interpreter), page tree, outline, forms/interactive, rendering/PageDrawer, text/PDFTextStripper; `fontbox` cmap, cff, ttf (TTFParser, GSUB), encoding; plus scans of xmpbox/preflight/examples/debugger for XML/deserialization/process/network primitives. The P1 index only returned navigation candidates (no data-flow, control-flow or semantic resolution) and omits 316 files, so index edges were not used as evidence. Not deeply reviewed: encryption/signature handlers, preflight validators, tools/debugger GUI code, most examples, and large parts of rendering/shading arithmetic.
limitations: No code execution, tests, scanners or exploit payloads were run; all findings are static source-level leads, not runtime-confirmed vulnerabilities.
The P1 relation index is partial (813/1,288 Java files parsed, 316 omitted, 30,296 unresolved calls) and has no data-flow/control-flow semantics; unreported areas were not assumed reviewed.
Binary/PDF test fixtures could not be read, so behavior against real crafted PDFs could not be validated.
The mapping to the benchmark's exact VUL4J-20 ground truth (CVE/fix commit) is uncertain; multiple plausible DoS root causes exist in this snapshot and only one candidate could be submitted.
One file was excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter and not inspected.

rejected_leads.lead: `CMap.readCode()` (fontbox/src/main/java/org/apache/fontbox/cmap/CMap.java lines 104-124) returns 0 consuming no bytes if a codespace range has length 0 (e.g. `begincodespacerange <> <> endcodespacerange` parsed by CMapParser), and `PDFStreamEngine.showText()` (pdfbox/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/contentstream/PDFStreamEngine.java lines 686-694) loops `while (in.available() > 0)` without checking `codeLength == 0` → infinite loop during text extraction/rendering.
rejected_leads.reason: Real and reachable (embedded CMaps are parsed via PDFont.readCMap → CMapManager), but it needs a Type0 font plus text-showing content, and I could not confirm whether it is the specific VUL4J-20 fix; kept as second-strongest lead, not the submitted candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Type 4 function interpreter: `InstructionSequence.execute()` trailing proc loop (lines 105-109) plus recursive `ConditionalOperators.If/IfElse.execute()` allow attacker-controlled PostScript-calculator functions to recurse or re-execute procs until StackOverflowError / long CPU burn.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires rendering/shading to invoke the function and a more elaborate crafted function stream; failure mode is a StackOverflowError rather than a clear no-progress spin, and no execution limit exists to cite as the fixed control.

rejected_leads.lead: `PDPageTree.PageIterator.enqueueKids()` (lines 162-176) and `get(int, COSDictionary, int)` (lines 239-298) recurse through `/Kids` with no visited-set, so a self-referencing page tree causes unbounded recursion/StackOverflowError.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible DoS but the failure is a fast StackOverflowError, and the source gives no direct evidence tying it to the benchmark case; unconfirmed as a CVE.

rejected_leads.lead: `PDFXrefStreamParser.parse()` (lines 91-100) expands `/Index` pairs (`for i < size: objNums.add(...)`) with attacker-controlled sizes and no bound, and `PDFObjectStreamParser.parse()` (lines 71-80) pre-allocates `ArrayList`s from `/N`; both allow tiny crafted PDFs to force OutOfMemoryError or a very long loop during parsing.
rejected_leads.reason: Strong DoS evidence, but impact is memory exhaustion / large allocation rather than the no-progress loop pattern, and I could not determine which (if any) upstream fix corresponds to this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: `CCITTFaxFilter.decode()` (lines 44-63) computes `arraySize = (cols + 7) / 8 * rows` from attacker-controlled `/Columns`/`/Rows` with int overflow/oversized allocation (NegativeArraySizeException or OOM).
rejected_leads.reason: Real unbounded-allocation issue, but it is a crash/OOM, not the zero-progress computation; no validation exists to cite as a fix, and reachability requires CCITT-encoded streams.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE / unsafe XML parsing (xmpbox, FDF/XFDF, XFA): DocumentBuilderFactory instances in `XMLUtil`, `PDXFAResource`, `DomXmpParser` already set `disallow-doctype-decl`, external general/parameter entities off.
rejected_leads.reason: Existing hardening contradicts an XXE finding; no vulnerable parser configuration found.

summary: Reviewed the Apache PDFBox snapshot (VUL4J-20, pdfbox 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT, no 2019+ files, latest referenced issues ~PDFBOX-4279). Scope filters: 1,492 visible files (1 excluded by sensitive-name/path filter; binary files skipped). The P1 relation index is partial (813/1,288 Java files parsed, 316 omitted; no data-flow/semantic resolution; 30,296 unresolved calls), so all conclusions come from source reading. I traced attacker-controlled PDF fields through the COS parser, stream filters, font/CMap handling, content-stream engine, page tree and Type 4 function interpreter. The single strongest, fully source-verifiable DoS is a zero-progress (infinite) loop in the predictor decoder: an attacker-controlled stream `/DecodeParms` dictionary can set the decoded row length to 0, after which `PredictorOutputStream.write()` never advances and never throws, so any consumer (including xref/object streams decoded during `PDDocument.load`) spins forever. Alternative unconfirmed leads are listed as rejected leads.
